public_rationale: The reported launch comparison rises from 25.4% to 38.6%, a substantial gain. This supports Marcus's reading of the tool-enabled configuration. It does not establish that symbolic code alone caused the gain: the toolkit also included search, and the public records do not fully document experimental controls.
limitations: Support is for the reported toolkit comparison, not an isolated causal effect of Python.
Numerical evidence comes from reputable launch reporting because the primary chart's values were unavailable in read_page text.
The Scientific American page was published July 11 and updated July 15; the later date is used conservatively.

our_interpretation: Assess the Grok 4 launch comparison discussed in the post.
Read 'dramatically' as a substantial increase in benchmark accuracy, without imposing an unstated numerical cutoff.
Read 'symbolic tools' as the tool-enabled configuration in the cited comparison, including code execution and search. This does not isolate the contribution of code execution.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable Grok 4 results on Humanity's Last Exam show a substantial accuracy increase when the reported toolkit is enabled.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable results show little improvement, no improvement, or worse accuracy with the toolkit enabled.
